subject: Career
title: ATS Ranking Algorithms
description: A quick, practical guide to ATS Ranking Algorithms.

hook.text: An ATS doesn't just filter — it ranks. Your resume gets a score compared to every other applicant.

buildup.text: Scoring weighs keyword frequency, recency of experience, title match, and sometimes education.

discovery.text: Recent experience with matching keywords scores higher than older, tangential roles.

twist.text: Some systems use AI now. They look beyond keywords at semantic meaning and context.

climax.text: The game is evolving. Exact matches still matter, but relevance is replacing repetition.

punchline.text: Don't just match keywords. Match the job.

quiz.question: What factors do ATS ranking algorithms typically weigh?

details.summary: ATS ranking algorithms score resumes based on keyword density, skills match percentage, experience recency, and job title alignment with the posted role. Understanding how these algorithms prioritize information lets you optimize your resume for maximum ranking.
details.whyItMatters: A small improvement in ATS ranking can mean the difference between appearing on the first page of candidates or never being seen by a human reviewer.
takeaways: Mirror the exact language from the job description in your resume
Recent experience is weighted more heavily than older experience
Job titles that closely match the posted role receive ranking boosts

faq.question: Does the order of keywords in your resume affect ATS ranking scores?
faq.answer: Most modern ATS systems weight keywords appearing in recent roles and prominent sections more heavily than those buried in older positions. Placing critical keywords in your summary and most recent experience sections maximizes their ranking impact.

faq.question: Can you game ATS ranking by stuffing keywords into your resume?
faq.answer: Keyword stuffing is detectable by modern ATS systems and is flagged as suspicious. Even if it passes the software, a human reviewer will immediately notice unnatural keyword density. Use keywords organically within descriptions of genuine experience and skills.
